body: Monday, August 03 2026 — Macro · Sectors · Flows · Crypto

Macro Stance: The Warsh-led Fed held rates steady at its July 29 meeting, but three dissents — all in favor of a hike — signal a deeply fractured committee. The 10Y yield is surging at 4.69% (+21 bps vs 4W), while the 2Y at 4.28% (prior close, +14 bps vs 4W) has risen less, producing a +47bps curve that is positively sloped but still flat by historical standards. Oil at 79.47 (↑15.9% vs 4W) is a new inflation input. The Fed explicitly cited the Iran war oil shock as context for the hold. Fiscal stance remains expansive; no new consolidation signals.

New / Most Important: The three-dissent hold was the most hawkish "pause" in years. Warsh stated the Fed "won't hesitate to stop inflation," yet the bond market is skeptical — Reuters notes the market is "scratching its head." Big Tech earnings (Amazon, Meta, Microsoft) surged, but the Nasdaq 100 at 28,720 is actually ↓3.3% vs 4W, suggesting the broader mega-cap complex is under distribution even as individual beats occur. The Leopold Aschenbrenner AI fund blowup — a 4x-leveraged vehicle losing 67% in a month after being up 439% — is a microcosm of the speculative froth now unwinding in AI-adjacent levered strategies. The S&P at 7,587 (↑0.7%) is diverging sharply from the Nasdaq, which is structurally new: this is a rotation out of duration-sensitive growth into value/cyclical, confirmed by Russell/Nasdaq ratio ↑2.1%.

Playbook ✓: Fed hold amid conflicting data; oil shock providing cover for hawkish inaction; curve steepening as long-end reprices term premium.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: The three-dissent hawkish hold is structurally unusual under the new Warsh Fed. This is the first time in the modern era that three FOMC members voted for a hike while the chair held — it suggests the committee's reaction function has shifted materially. The market is not pricing a hike (VIX at 15.6 screams complacency), but the option space is mispriced if Warsh himself rotates toward the dissenters on the next inflation print. The fact that the 10Y is surging while equities are broadly flat means the bond market is doing the tightening the Fed won't — a classic late-cycle dynamic where the term premium becomes the policy tool. The Iran war oil spike layered onto this creates a stagflationary whiff that consensus has not yet internalized.

Macro Stance: Eurozone inflation surprised to the upside at 2.9% in July, reigniting the case for a September ECB rate hike. The ECB wage tracker shows no pickup in wage pressures, creating a split signal — headline inflation driven by energy, not embedded wage-price spiral. Euro and Bund yields are firming on the data. Money supply growth is rising while lending stays steady.

New / Most Important: The July CPI print at 2.9% is the critical development. Markets are now pricing a September hike as "more likely" per Morningstar. This is a reversal — as recently as June, the consensus was that the ECB's tightening cycle was done. The energy channel (oil ↑15.9%) is the primary transmission mechanism, meaning this is an imported inflation shock, not demand-driven — a crucial distinction the ECB historically struggles with. European stocks advanced as oil eased intraday, but the medium-term setup is adversarial for European risk if the ECB tightens into a supply shock.

Playbook ✓: Energy-driven inflation overshoot forcing hawkish ECB repricing — textbook supply-shock passthrough.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: The ECB wage tracker showing NO pickup is deeply at odds with the headline CPI move. This creates a policy trap: if the ECB hikes into a pure supply shock with no wage acceleration, it risks crushing demand without addressing the source of inflation. This is the 2022 playbook repeating, but now with even less fiscal room in the periphery. The "great betrayal of the London stock market" narrative from The Telegraph signals capital continuing to flee European listed equity markets structurally. If the ECB hikes while the Fed holds, the EUR strengthening becomes self-defeating — a tighter financial condition overlay on already weak industrial activity.

Macro Stance: The PBOC has answered the July data with words, not yet with cuts. It pledged timely adjustment of its policy tools (Reuters, [Aug 2]) and a moderately loose stance backed by more effective incremental measures in H2 (Global Times, [Aug 2]), with ample liquidity to be maintained (finance.biggo.com, [Aug 2]); one read of the Politburo is that RRR and rate cuts are likely in Q3 (BigGo Finance, [Jul 30]). The overnight reverse repo rate stayed at 1.25% (Reuters, [Jul 28]). The currency is the constraint: the yuan hit a three-year high despite the PBOC signalling discomfort (The Edge Malaysia, [Jul 31]), and Rabobank argues the rally may lose momentum (Exchange Rates UK, [Aug 2]), while the forex regulator pledged to open up the market and tighten capital oversight (South China Morning Post, [Aug 2]). June CPI rose only 1% (Global Times, [Jul 9]) while PPI climbed 4.1% (finance.biggo.com, [Jul 8]), a margin squeeze rather than reflation.

PMIs & Activity: The two July surveys diverge in level but agree in direction. The official manufacturing PMI dropped to 49.2 (The State Council Information Office, [Jul 31]) and non-manufacturing to 49 (Macau Business, [Jul 31]), as factories and construction slumped together (The Edge Malaysia, [Jul 31]); the private survey still shows factory growth, but at a four-month low (Reuters, [Aug 2]). Reconciled: the export-oriented private sample is slowing, the broader official sample with its construction and domestic weight is contracting, and Bloomberg reads it as a slump that reinforces signs of slowdown ([Aug 2]). Against June's 50.3 (Reuters, [Jun 29]) the break is clear. Q2 GDP grew 4.3%, below the target range (Bloomberg, [Jul 15]), first-half industrial profits rose 18.7% as a tech boom masks the property slump (Caixin Global, [Jul 27]), and US-bound shipments fell in July (CNBC, [Jul 30]).

Credit Impulse: June new bank loans rose less than expected (The Star, [Jul 15]) and credit growth missed forecasts as the PBOC flagged a "new normal" (Caixin Global, [Jul 16]); household loans fell by 366.8 billion yuan in the first half (36Kr, [Jul 17]). Cash at Chinese banks has swelled to a record as borrowing slows (Nikkei Asia, [Jul 28]): liquidity is ample, credit demand is not, which is why "ample liquidity" pledges change little. A dip in the debt ratio may not bode well for the economy (South China Morning Post, [Jul 31]), even as the local government debt clean-up makes progress (ISI Markets, [Aug 1]). The impulse reads flat, with households negative.

Property: June new home prices fell at a slower pace (Reuters, [Jul 14]) and first-tier prices extended a four-month rebound (South China Morning Post, [Jul 15]), but resale prices fell faster (Reuters, [Jun 30]) and property investment slumped 18 percent y/y in January–June (The Standard (HK), [Jul 15]). Households are walking away from homes and into portfolios (South China Morning Post, [Aug 1]) and July was the worst building month since Covid (Wood Central, [Aug 1]). The contrarian bid is commercial: investors are snapping up prime office space on a rebound bet (South China Morning Post, [Aug 2]).

Fiscal, Policy & Trade: The Politburo settled on incremental policy support (Caixin Global, [Jul 31]), a fiscal push without big stimulus (VT Markets, [Jul 31]); leaders pledged support without big new stimulus plans (Reuters, [Jul 30]), while Bloomberg reports officials will consider new stimulus after the slowdown ([Jul 30]). Reconciled: incremental measures now, more only if data worsen. On trade, China drew "red lines" around its economic model ahead of EU and US talks (Reuters, [Aug 2]), a stance Bloomberg warns will come at a cost ([Aug 2]); the US urged China to "fully meet" its rare-earths pledge (Nikkei Asia, [Jul 31]) as a Trump-Xi September summit takes shape (Firstpost, [Jul 31]).

Markets & Flows: Semiconductors are the dominant lens. CXMT surged 466% on its Shanghai debut (Reuters, [Jul 27]), though The Business Times calls the US$10 billion IPO a flop ([Jul 28]): the first-day pop measured domestic capital's appetite for chip self-sufficiency, not post-listing returns. Yahoo Finance frames it as leverage for Apple against Micron, and global semiconductor stocks pared losses amid fears of Chinese competition. Onshore, Chinese stocks were on track for their worst month in a decade (Financial Times, [Jul 30]), while Hong Kong rallied 3.7% on a five-day winning streak (BusinessToday Malaysia, [Aug 2]) and the CSRC unveiled measures to deepen mainland-HK market ties (chinadailyhk, [Aug 2]).

New / Most Important: The PBOC's H2 guidance is the policy answer to July: timely tool adjustment, moderately loose, ample liquidity. With the official PMI in contraction and the private gauge at a four-month low, that reads as a door opened to RRR and rate cuts. The constraint is that liquidity is not the bottleneck, as record bank cash shows, and a strong yuan already tightens conditions for exporters.

Playbook ✓: Domestic capital channelled into strategic tech, incremental easing and weak property are on script.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: Asia's other factories are firming, with South Korea's activity quickening on export demand (Reuters, [Aug 2]), while China's PMIs slide, so the drag is Chinese domestic demand rather than global trade. That concentrates the hit on China-specific channels: iron ore eased as faltering China demand offset stimulus hopes (Business Recorder, [Jul 28]), AUD and NZD stay exposed after NZD/USD slipped on weak China PMIs (VT Markets, [Jul 31]), and European exporters face a deepening China slump. The #PapergamesRuinsCNgaming hashtag trending on US Twitter is a reminder that Chinese tech sentiment abroad is deteriorating even as domestic capital piles in. Oil at $79.47 remains a terms-of-trade tax on China's margins.

Macro Stance: The BOJ held rates at 1% on July 31 but warned core inflation is exceeding its 2% target and explicitly "nodded to the chance of an early rate hike." The yen is climbing against both the dollar and euro as traders speculate on further intervention. A coordinated US-Japan intervention framework has been revealed by Reuters.

New / Most Important: The US-Japan yen intervention pact is the most structurally significant development in G10 FX this week. Reuters detailed "how a US-Japan pact to hit yen speculators came together" — this is the first formal bilateral currency intervention agreement in decades and represents a fundamental shift in the FX policy architecture. The BOJ committed to more rate hikes with the weak yen cited as a key inflation transmission channel. Toyota reports earnings today with expectations of higher revenue despite global sales slippage — the weak yen has been a profit buffer, but that tailwind is now reversing. Business Insider notes traders are "glued to one trade" — the yen carry unwind. This is the most crowded and dangerous position in macro right now. If the BOJ hikes earlier than expected and the intervention pact holds, the carry trade unwind could cascade through EM and US credit markets where yen-funded positions are embedded.

Playbook ✓: BOJ gradually normalizing; yen intervention when weakness threatens imported inflation.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: The bilateral US-Japan intervention pact is the divergence — this is NOT in any standard playbook. The US actively participating in strengthening a foreign currency against the dollar is extraordinary and suggests Washington views yen weakness as a geopolitical vulnerability (Japan's defense spending requires a stable yen) rather than a purely economic issue. This has massive implications for the carry trade, for US Treasury demand (Japan is the largest foreign holder), and for the dollar's role as the unilateral FX anchor. If the US is now willing to co-intervene for allied currencies, the entire G10 FX regime is shifting.

Macro Stance: Inflation undershot forecasts at 3.8%, materially reducing the probability of an RBA rate hike. Markets axed rate hike bets following the data. Governor Bullock left the threat of higher rates on the table rhetorically but the data isn't supporting it.

New / Most Important: The inflation undershoot is the week's key event — traders immediately pared hike bets. Housing market eased "more than anticipated" per the RBA. The combination of softer CPI and cooling housing removes the two pillars that were supporting the hike case.

Playbook ✓: Data-dependent hold; inflation gravitating lower removes urgency.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: Some economists still warn rate rises are coming (AFR), creating a non-trivial gap between market pricing and a subset of forecasters. With oil surging 15.9%, Australia's terms-of-trade improvement (as a commodity exporter) may paradoxically reignite demand-side pressures in Q3, making the current dovish repricing premature.

Macro Stance: A split is opening at the top of the NBP. Super Biznes [Aug 3] reports Glapiński wants to lower rates and that experts are sounding the alarm, days after GUS's flash put July CPI at 3.0% y/y (Miesięcznik Finansowy BANK, [Jul 31]) on fuel prices up roughly 14% in a month (Obserwator Gospodarczy, [Jul 31]) once the government's fuel shield expired (Magazyn MANAGER+, [Aug 1]). The Rzeczpospolita and Parkiet economist panels [Jul 31] argued the Council should not hurry, and Citi's call of above 3.5% by year-end still constrains the easing path. Today's data cut the other way for the doves: the manufacturing PMI rebounded in July with the first rise in employment for months, though still below the growth threshold (Rzeczpospolita and BIZNES24, [Aug 3]), and GUS statistics show Poland growing twice as fast as the EU as a whole (Agro Profil, [Jul 31]). The NBP's credit survey says banks will tighten for households and loosen for firms (Money.pl and Direct Money, [Aug 3]), a quiet form of tightening the Council does not have to vote on. Stance: hold, but a governor talking cuts with CPI at 3% is the new variable.

Markets: WIG20 closed at an all-time high, beating the peak from almost two decades ago (Parkiet and TVN24, [Aug 3]); StockWatch.pl [Aug 3] put Orlen, PKO BP and Żabka at the centre of the record session, while PGE led the gains and Allegro was the weakest blue chip (Inwestycje.pl, [Aug 3]). The move is energy-led: Strefa Biznesu [Aug 3] lists companies beyond Orlen that gain from dear fuel, and the card shows PGE 10.11 (+5.0% 4W) and Orlen 148.04 (+11.4% 4W, -5.1% 1W) with Comparic [Aug 3] asking whether Orlen's pause after the rally is a buying opportunity. The rest of the card (prior session): PKO 111.92 (+5.0% 1W, +6.3% 4W), Pekao 245.5 (+5.0% 1W), Dino 31.99 (+11.2% 1W, +15.5% 4W), LPP 21,720 (+7.8% 1W, +17.1% 4W), CD Projekt 249.9 (+10.5% 1W), Allegro 44.99 (+17.0% 4W), KGHM 307.95 (-8.1% 4W); EPOL 42.83 is +4.7% 1W and +8.6% 4W. The zloty caught a geopolitical bid: Trump announced a halt to the attack on Iran and oil fell (OKO.press, [Aug 3]), Bankier [Aug 3] reports the zloty reacting positively to talk of a new Iran deal with the euro lower, and FXMAG [Aug 3] has the zloty gaining more than 6 grosz against the dollar. The card has USD/PLN 3.7286 (-1.5% 1W, -0.5% 4W) and EUR/PLN 4.304 (-0.2% 1W, +0.4% 4W). No fresh POLGB headlines today.

Fiscal & Politics: Defence is the new spending priority: Domański said the government will strongly support defence investment and needs as much of it as possible (WNP.PL, [Aug 3]), while the finance ministry published how long repayment of the EU SAFE loan will take (Fakt and Do Rzeczy, [Aug 3]). The MF has withdrawn its controversial tax changes, with Interia [Aug 3] checking what remains in the draft; bottled water keeps its 23% VAT rate for the good of the budget (Podatki.biz, [Aug 3]). The Sejm granted discharge for the 2025 budget (Prawo.pl, [Jul 31]) against debt above 2 trillion zł (naTemat.pl, [Jul 27]); the president is pushing a deficit hammer with penalties for overspending politicians (BitHub.pl, [Aug 1]). Fuel politics has shifted from caps to arm-twisting: the government wants to force Orlen to cut pump prices and widen promotions (Next Gazeta.pl, [Aug 3]) with the minister pointing to minimal margins (Bankier, [Aug 3]); the CPN package itself has no financing after the president's decision (Money.pl, [Jul 31]).

Corporate & Sectors: Energy: Enea, PGE, Orlen and Unimot signed up to the FSRU2 floating LNG terminal (Bankier, [Aug 3]); Poland's largest power plant is running without a key unit (Business Insider Polska, [Aug 3]) and e-magazyny.pl [Aug 3] expects spot power above 2000 zł per MWh on Tuesday evening, while Rzeczpospolita [Aug 3] sees Poland becoming a power exporter as Hungary shuts the Paks nuclear plant for lack of Danube water. KGHM's Nitroerg will invest 300 million zł in explosives for defence (Bankier, [Aug 3]). Banks: Pekao beat forecasts despite lower rates and higher CIT (Rzeczpospolita, [Jul 30]), mBank posted a record result (Gazeta Prawna, [Jul 29]), mortgages ran above 13 bn zł for a fourth month (Rzeczpospolita, [Jul 30]); Money.pl [Aug 3] says the state sided with banks on interest for undisbursed funds. Retail: the Żabka takeover is worth 32.62 bn zł (Yahoo Finance, [Aug 3]); Dino is rebounding after a difficult first half (DlaHandlu.pl, [Aug 3]) with union mediation resuming (Farmer.pl, [Aug 1]); an appeals court ordered Allegro to unlock the full view of delivery options (NowyMarketing, [Aug 3]) as Allegro reported buyback trades; LPP sought admission of series N shares (Strefa Inwestorów, [Aug 3]).

Geopolitics & Security: Belarus is sending special forces to the Ukrainian border on Lukashenko's order and forming a new assault brigade (Polskie Radio 24 and Forsal.pl, [Aug 3]); TVP World [Aug 3] reports Russian plans to use captured Ukrainian drones to provoke NATO after last week's Kh-101 crash in the Lublin region, and the defence minister said Russia's war stocks are exhausted (Rzeczpospolita, [Jul 31]).

New / Most Important: The 2007 ceiling is gone. WIG20's close above a high that stood for almost two decades, on the same day Trump paused the Iran strikes and oil fell, matters because it changes who owns Polish equities: the index is now a breakout, not a value trade. The risk is that the breakout is energy-led while the government leans on Orlen's margins and the governor floats cuts into a 3% CPI, so leadership could rotate back to banks quickly. With WTI having run 15.9% into this, the Iran pause is the single input that makes the record sustainable.

Playbook ✓: Hold pattern as inflation risks persist; stay long GPW with a bank core and treat Orlen on any government-imposed price cut as the hedge.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: Glapiński's cut talk versus the Council's panels — if the governor wins, the zloty's Iran-driven bid reverses and the import channel for inflation reopens.
Macro Stance: The SBP held its policy rate at 11.5%, citing inflation and geopolitical risks as limiting easing room. Oil-importing EM remains the most vulnerable cohort to the Iran war energy shock.

New / Most Important: The hold was expected but the explicit mention of geopolitical risks as a constraint is notable — Pakistan sits in the direct transmission zone of Middle East instability.  |  Playbook ✓: Oil-importing EM central banks forced to hold despite growth headwinds.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: None today.

Narrative: Big Tech beats drove strong single-stock moves, but the Nasdaq 100 is ↓3.3% vs 4W — distribution beneath the surface — as a 10Y at 4.69% weighs on duration and the Aschenbrenner AI fund implosion purges AI-adjacent excess.

Reported: Apple dropped the most in 16 months on a disappointing outlook (AFR, [Aug 1]) after a forecast dogged by supply-chain struggles (Reuters, [Jul 30]). Microsoft beat with $90B in revenue and its shares jumped 9% (KOMO, [Jul 29]), saying cash will keep flowing from AI (Reuters, [Jul 31]). Fair Isaac plunged 17% on mixed results and a delay in a key program (TIKR.com, [Jul 31]).

EPS Upside Watch: Palantir — goes into its report with 8 straight beats, 40% off its high, and options pricing a 12% swing (TradingKey, [Aug 2]). Unity Software — earnings are expected to grow (Yahoo Finance, [Jul 30]), and the shares may move 11% on the August release (Investing.com, [Jul 30]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: The Nasdaq trailing the S&P by ~400bps over four weeks despite strong Big Tech earnings is a regime signal: mega-cap beats usually lift the index mechanically, so their failure to do so points to institutional selling into strength — the Mag 7 did a split, and the rotation may be structural.

Narrative: AI infrastructure spend is flowing through communication platforms as ad targeting improves, and Alphabet, Amazon and Microsoft added nearly $1.5 trillion in combined value in the week (CNBC, [Jul 31]).

Reported: Meta's profit missed estimates on higher costs (Yahoo Finance UK, [Jul 29]), and its stock fell 7.5% as investors fretted over more expenses (TradingView, [Jul 30]). Reddit sank 11% on 'choppy' search referrals even as its results blew past estimates (CNBC, [Jul 30]). Telus slumped after slashing its dividend and cutting its 2026 outlook (StocksToTrade, [Aug 1]).

EPS Upside Watch: Verizon — analysts raised their forecasts after its better-than-expected Q2 (Benzinga, [Jul 27]). Sony — raised guidance as its Q1 profit beat on a strong gaming business (Reuters, [Jul 30]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: Big Tech earnings are sending valuations in opposite directions (WSJ, [Aug 2]): Meta's spending without a matching revenue lift is de-rated while Alphabet is paid, so the bullish call is a stock-picking one, not sector beta.

Narrative: A steepening curve (+47bps 10Y-2Y, 12 bps wider over four weeks) is a modestly improving NIM environment, though still flat by historical standards; UBS's $153M in AML fines is idiosyncratic but recalls the post-Credit Suisse compliance tightening.

Reported: Deutsche Bank's profit rose 10%, defying an expected decline, as its investment bank boomed (Reuters, [Jul 29]). MUFG beat estimates to seal a strong quarter for Japan banks (Yahoo Finance Singapore, [Aug 2]). Barclays' profit rose 17% on an equities boom, but its shares fell as costs are set to rise (Reuters, [Jul 28]).

EPS Upside Watch: PayPal — raised full-year EPS guidance (Yahoo Finance, [Jul 28]), and analysts boosted their forecasts after the upbeat Q2 (Benzinga, [Jul 29]). Mastercard — topped Q2 estimates, and analysts see more upside despite an early stock dip (Benzinga, [Jul 31]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: The curve is positive and the inverted-curve recession crowd has so far been wrong, yet XLF has not dramatically outperformed: the market is pricing credit losses that have not materialized. With banks beating, watch for that disconnect to close.

Narrative: WTI at 79.47 (↑15.9% vs 4W) reflects the Iran war supply shock, and with China's private factory gauge at a four-month low and the official PMI in contraction this is supply, not demand; Mideast deal hopes eased prices intraday, but the disruption premium persists.

Reported: Chevron posted its highest quarterly profit in six years and beat estimates (Reuters, [Jul 31]) as refining margins soared, while rival Exxon missed (Yahoo Finance, [Jul 31]) and its stock dropped after the miss (TIKR.com, [Aug 2]). Shell's profit more than doubled to $9.8 billion, its second-highest on record, as the Iran war lifted prices (Reuters, [Jul 30]).

EPS Upside Watch: Targa Resources — expected to beat earnings estimates into its Q2 release (Yahoo Finance, [Jul 30]). SLB — raised its outlook as data-centre revenue leapt 80%, and analysts lifted price targets (BigGo Finance, [Jul 27]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: European stocks advanced precisely because oil eased, an inverse link with oil tighter than at any point since 2022. That makes long XLE / short STOXX 600 a clean expression of the geopolitical risk premium.

Narrative: Industrials gain from the rotation out of tech into cyclicals — the Russell/Nasdaq ratio ↑2.1% confirms breadth favouring industrial-heavy small and mid caps — and copper ↑5.9% supports the AI data-centre and grid-capex story.

Reported: Schneider Electric lifted its 2026 outlook as data-centre demand surged (Reuters, [Jul 30]). Quanta Services jumped 17% after topping consensus estimates and raising guidance (TIKR.com, [Jul 31]). Parsons faced guidance cuts on portfolio reshaping and delays (Yahoo Finance, [Aug 1]).
EPS Upside Watch: Proto Labs — lifted guidance on new data-centre and defence clients (Bloomberg.com, [Jul 31]). Axon — expected to beat earnings estimates (Yahoo Finance, [Jul 29]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: The AI boom is lifting industrial stocks (Axios, [Jul 31]), so the old-economy sector now carries tech-style multiple risk, while UPS dropping on a Q3 revenue warning after a beat and raised outlook (Tech Times, [Jul 28]) shows the non-AI half gets no such credit.
Narrative: Amazon's strong earnings are a tailwind, but rising oil acts as a consumer tax, leaving the sector caught between strong corporate results and energy-squeezed purchasing power.

Reported: Amazon soared 12% (Yahoo Finance, [Jul 31]) after lifting investment plans on strong cloud sales (Reuters, [Jul 31]), and JPMorgan reset its target after the AI payoff (TheStreet, [Aug 2]). Chipotle jumped as it hiked its same-store sales forecast (CNBC, [Jul 29]). Crocs beat sales expectations, but the stock dropped 12.7% (StockStory, [Jul 30]).
EPS Upside Watch: Cracker Barrel — earnings estimates are rising (Yahoo Finance, [Jul 31]). Starbucks — CNBC is raising its price target after a home-run quarter (CNBC, [Jul 29]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: Amazon's surge is a cloud and AI story booked in a consumer sector; strip it out and the prints are cost-squeezed — Chipotle's beef and labor costs cut restaurant margin 220 basis points (Pulse 2.0, [Aug 2]) even as comparable sales rose.
Narrative: Defensive positioning benefits from the tech-to-value rotation; rising yields usually hurt staples' dividend appeal, but the geopolitical fear premium is overriding the rate sensitivity.

Reported: Coca-Cola beat Q2 forecasts and its shares jumped 6% (Investing.com, [Jul 28]) as it raised guidance on a World Cup sales lift (Bloomberg.com, [Jul 28]). Procter & Gamble beat estimates but the stock fell (Barron's, [Jul 29]) as it forecast slower annual sales growth with costs weighing (Reuters, [Jul 29]). Colgate beat on strong margins as sales rose 4.9% (Yahoo Finance, [Jul 31]).
EPS Upside Watch: Tyson Foods — analysts predict a rise in its third-quarter earnings (Northwest Arkansas Democrat-Gazette, [Jul 31]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: The haven is priced like growth: Coca-Cola hit an all-time high with a P/E now topping some AI leaders (BigGo Finance, [Jul 28]) while Q3 estimates are falling for consumer staples (Yahoo Finance, [Jul 29]). The bid runs ahead of the earnings, so cost-hit prints like P&G's get sold.

Narrative: Eli Lilly faces a "key test" as the GLP-1 story reaches an earnings inflection, Amgen's data breach adds cybersecurity risk to biopharma valuations, and JNJ's surgical robotics milestone is a positive catalyst.

Reported: Bristol Myers Squibb raised its 2026 forecast after a Q2 beat (Quartz, [Jul 30]). AbbVie's sales beat as Botox showed signs of revival (Bloomberg.com, [Jul 31]), but its shares were pressured as the beat fell below investor expectations (BioSpace, [Jul 31]). Alnylam tanked 28% on a Q2 miss and a cut to its 2026 sales view (Yahoo Finance, [Jul 31]).

EPS Upside Watch: Biogen — beat as new medicines overtake its MS business (Bloomberg.com, [Jul 29]) and raised 2026 guidance (Zacks Investment Research, [Jul 29]). Labcorp — raised its earnings outlook on strong medical testing demand (Bloomberg.com, [Jul 30]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: Biotech is a stock-picker's market, not a beta trade: of three noteworthy biotechs only one recovered after earnings, and guidance cuts at Alnylam and Boston Scientific, which cut 2026 guidance again despite Q2 beats (MassDevice, [Jul 29]), sit beside raises at Bristol Myers and Biogen.

Narrative: Copper at 6.54 (↑5.9% vs 4W) is the primary signal — demand for the AI data-centre and grid-capex metal stays firm while China's construction-heavy demand does not, with the non-manufacturing PMI at 49 in July — and with gold at 4,093 (↓1.5%) cooling, the edge sits with copper miners as an AI and grid-capex play.

Reported: Rio Tinto posted a 43% jump in first-half earnings as the data-centre boom boosted copper (Reuters, [Jul 29]). Linde beat Q2 forecasts on strong electronics demand and lifted its outlook (Reuters, [Jul 31]). Corteva raised its full-year profit forecast, but its shares fell after a revenue miss (Reuters, [Jul 30]).
